title: THE WEIGHT NO ONE CAN CARRY ALONE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth? Why do you tell me to carry them in my arms, as a nurse carries an infant, to the land you promised on oath to their ancestors? Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep wailing to me, "Give us meat to eat!" I cannot carry all these people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me. — Num 11:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses lays out exactly why he is drowning. The people are behaving like demanding infants, and he feels expected to be their mother, nurse, and provider all at once. "Did I give them birth?" he cries. In other words: "These are not even mine to carry, and yet the whole weight has landed on me."

His words are painfully relatable. Many of us have felt the burden of responsibility for people whose needs are endless and whose gratitude is thin. Moses reaches an important, humbling truth: "I cannot carry all these people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me."

That confession is not weakness — it is wisdom. God never designed one person to carry everything. The moment we admit we cannot do it alone is often the moment help arrives. Pride keeps us struggling in silence; humility opens the door to the support God wants to send.

There is only One who can truly carry all people — and it is not Moses, and it is not you. It is Christ, who bore the weight of the whole world's sin upon the cross. When you feel the crushing pull of "it all depends on me," remember it never did. Lay it down before the One whose shoulders are strong enough.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What responsibility are you trying to carry that was never meant for you alone?
2. Why is it hard for you to admit "this is too heavy for me"?
3. How does knowing Christ carries all things bring you relief today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess the burdens I have tried to carry alone. Thank You that Christ bore what I never could. Teach me humility to ask for help and trust in Your strength. Amen.
